Class KWebGraphC3D

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.sg.SceneGraphObject
org.jdesktop.lg3d.sg.Node
org.jdesktop.lg3d.sg.Group
org.jdesktop.lg3d.sg.BranchGroup
org.jdesktop.lg3d.wg.Component3D
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.kwebdemo1.components.KWebGraphC3D
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.jdesktop.lg3d.wg.event.LgEventSource
public class KWebGraphC3D extends org.jdesktop.lg3d.wg.Component3D
The component that handles the KWeb graph animations. This class can move, rotate and selectively show different parts of the KWeb graph. It also setups up event listeners, actions that are to take place when an animation finishes.

Implementation: Apparently, there are two ways to do animations: (1) using Component3D methods, (2) using AnimationGroups. The former is easier but I could not get the finished animation events to work with that approach. In fact, I got an error that prevented the animation from running at all when attempting to setup the finish event. Therefore, I ended up using the AnimationGroup approach. However, setting up the finish event handling using the AnimationGroup is less than obvious because there's no direct mechanism to setup an event Listener. In turns out that one can setup a listener by going through the LgEventConnnector class.

Since:
JDK 1.5.0, Java3D 1.4.0, lg3d-{core,demo,incubator} 0.7.0

    • startSlowRotation

      public void startSlowRotation()
      Runs an animation that slowly rotates the KWeb graph. This was specifically regquested by James Burke. The KWebGraph will continously rotate once every 100 seconds until stopped by stopSlowRotation. There are no events associated with this animation.

      While this animation is running, I don't think LG lets you running any of the event driven animations or change the appearance of the graph. I might be wrong, but it seems that way to me. Anyway, you should stop this particular animation when it's time to do real stuff.

    • stopSlowRotation

      public void stopSlowRotation()
      Stops the animation started by startSlowRotation. Then rotates the KWeb graph more rapidly and by the shortest rotation back to its initial starting point.

      Implementation: We do this by getting the Transform3D of the AnimationGroup. From there I get the 3x3 rotation matrix. Because the rotation is around the y-axis the top row is all we need which is a unit vector of (x, 0, z). The longitude is then obtained from arctan(z/x). We plug that in as the starting point for the return-to-zero animation and run a 10 second animation that returns to KWeb back to longitute 0 facing the viewer. m00 is x; m02 is z. I tried using this.getFinalRotationAngle() but it always returns 0.0, most likely because it assumes we are using the Component3D rotation methods which we are not.

    • createOneLinerC3D

      public org.jdesktop.lg3d.wg.Component3D createOneLinerC3D(NodeData nd, String oneLiner)
      Creates the one liner Component3D. This approach isn't consistent with the other Component3D creations, but I needed to access some internal data within the KWebGraphC3D component, so it's created with that fact in mind. I may change my mind later and create by subclassing Component3D in the same way the other components are created.
      Parameters:
      nd - reference to NodeData instance since KWebGraphC3D already has it
      oneLiner - default one liner displayed before anything is selected.
      Returns:
      an instance of the one liner component.
